1:56 to 75mm: Vehicle Scale Up to Display

A 2.62x upscale that turns a small wargaming vehicle into a substantial display piece, smoothing the surface for painting practice.

The math

(75.0mm / 28.6mm) × 100 = 262.2%

Based on 175cm human baseline, eye-level measurement (160cm).

Scale baselines

  • Source eye level28.6mm Eye
  • Target eye level75.0mm Eye
  • Scale factor262.2%

Display repurposing

At 262.2% a 1:56 tank becomes a large, smooth-canvas showpiece. The source's wargaming simplification works in its favour here — broad, flat panels perfect for blending and weathering practice.

A serious build

2.62x is a lot. It will almost certainly be a multi-part, large-print job. I plan sections, print at a fine profile, and expect a real time and material investment for a worthwhile display result.

How I got this number

By kitsorix, 3D printing hobbyist

This percentage comes from a 175cm human baseline with eye-level at 160cm. I print the result on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini and measure with digital calipers before I post it.

I test every percentage on FDM before publishing. PLA and PETG cool with minimal dimensional change — typically under 0.5%. If a number fails on my machine, I adjust it.

Quick Answers

Is 1:56 to 75mm worth it?

For a display study piece yes — 262.2% produces a broad, smooth canvas that is ideal for painting practice on a recognizable vehicle.
